conclusions: Nearby anonymous RX allocation is possible in a disposable WebProcess. The allocation helper enumerates unmapped gaps and uses mmap with a hint, never MAP_FIXED; it refuses out-of-range results. No installed binary changes.

Post-store-near control confirms a deliberate diagnostic x10=0 stop while real d0/d1 and stored slot equal 1. Ten real near-guard runs pass with FCSEL/FCMP/B.VS/STR left at original addresses; only RET is redirected.

Relocating FCSEL to a nearby three-instruction body (FCSEL, NOP, return branch) also passes ten attempts. Original comparison/store remain in place. The branch-based alternative is implemented and assembler-audited but has NOT been run in this record.
Entry-only control, without allocation or selection/store changes, fails on its first attempt at iteration 8461 slot 4, staged 2048 but array/local +0. Nine later attempts were not run.

Allocation-only control, with exactly the same near allocation but no engine payload or instruction writes, passes ten attempts. A later entry-only bracket also passes ten attempts. These small samples cannot establish allocation as the cause of suppression; they rule out attributing passes uniquely to the selection patch.
Across both entry-only batches there are ten passes and one genuine failure. All actual attempts are recorded; no retries. All startup JIT observations false and developer VM observations true.

Pinned static disassembly shows llint_op_new_array calls llint_slow_path_new_array, which calls constructArrayNegativeIndexed, whose loop calls JSObject::initializeIndex. This is binary call-chain evidence, not a capture of the failing instruction.
array_store_guard.S is an assembled/audited prospective stored-slot guard, not installed or used by these runs. Existing near guards compare conversion registers and only read slot memory on a stop.
No native array conversion mismatch captured and no production fix established. Passing instrumentation controls are not release qualification.
